summary: Josh Lloyd finishes his positional tier series with center-eligible players, using Fantrax eligibility and his own head-to-head ranking system. Nikola Jokic and Victor Wembanyama are tier one, with Jokic his slight pick at number one. Giannis Antetokounmpo is alone in tier two, and Scottie Barnes and Karl-Anthony Towns make up tier three. He thinks Chet Holmgren, Walker Kessler and Donovan Clingan are badly overdrafted, and that Rudy Gobert, Isaiah Hartenstein and Khaman Maluach give similar production much later. He says not to draft or stash the injured Mark Williams. He also says his tiers are not a draft bible and his opinions change as new information comes in.

rules.text: Tiers are a guide only. Do not treat them as a drafting bible.
rules.quote: you treat this as some sort of drafting bible. It is not is not.

rules.text: Rankings are fluid. The speaker changes his opinion daily as new information comes in, and you should debate your own rankings while staying uncertain.
rules.quote: So doubting and debating with yourself and with others while being uncertain of how things play out

rules.text: His head-to-head ranking system pushes centers down. In H2H you want to max out games played, so low turnovers matter less, and traditional box score values overrate blocks, steals and some percentages.
rules.quote: because in head-to-head leagues, you are trying to max out games played, meaning the impact of low turnovers

rules.text: Standard 9-cat rankings ('fluff') inflate some players, and those players get overdrafted. Be aware of that.
rules.quote: Tier seven has a lot of the guys that are going to be overdrafted thanks to nine capat fluffery.

rules.text: Roto and head-to-head are very different. Injury-risk stars like Embiid were worth taking in roto, but less so in H2H.
rules.quote: But Roto is very different to headto-head.

rules.text: Only take a high-injury-risk player late if you have not already taken anything super risky earlier in the draft.
rules.quote: take a you can take a chance if you haven't done anything super risky earlier on.

rules.text: Prefer a player with top 50 upside over a safe, boring player with a capped ceiling at the same draft spot.
rules.quote: The answer is you want the bloke who could be top 50.

rules.text: Do not draft or stash a long-term injured player. Only keep him in an empty injured slot and drop him once you need the spot.
rules.quote: If you have Mark Williams and you got no one else in your injured slot, hold him there

rules.text: Several late-tier centers are only worth looking at in 14-team leagues, not in 12-team leagues.
rules.quote: make sure you're looking at them in 14 cuz in a 12 team, I don't know what the point would be

rules.text: Players with similar category profiles (rebounds, blocks, FG%) should be drafted around the same area. Huge ADP gaps between them are market inefficiencies.
rules.quote: is ridiculous to me when they all should be around the same area.
